derivations.claim: The selected finite invariant-quotient/on-shell-equivalence interpretation carries the full-AC premise [A1]. Separately, by [F2] and [A3], the complete derivative-free holomorphic chiral integrand satisfies $F_\lambda(\Phi,W)=F_{\Lambda_0}(\Phi,W)$ coefficientwise for every formal perturbative order. Setting $W=0$ and restricting to the fixed light-field variables preserves this identity, so $W_\lambda(\Phi)=W_{\Lambda_0}(\Phi)$.

The map $P_{\mathrm{hol}}$ is the same linear coordinate projection at both scales by [A2]. Applying it to the equality in step 1.1 gives $P_{\mathrm{hol}}W_\lambda=P_{\mathrm{hol}}W_{\Lambda_0}$. Since the retained operators are a fixed ordered basis, equality of their coordinate vectors gives equality of each retained coefficient.

The gauge-coupling correction and the freedom of the real D-term are exactly the exceptions in [F2]. The conclusion concerns the fixed Wilsonian holomorphic coordinates, so it does not imply equality of one-particle-irreducible vertices or of coefficients after a scale-dependent field rescaling; the formal perturbative hypothesis in [A3] also excludes nonperturbative and continuum conclusions.

derivations.claim: Vary the terms depending on $X$ in the canonical superspace action. In the chiral coordinates $y=x+i\theta\sigma\bar\theta$ from [F2], define the ordered barred coefficient projector $\mathscr P_{\bar\theta}U=\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot2}}\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot1}}U|_{\bar\theta=0}$, with the derivatives taken at fixed $y,\theta$. The coefficient-extraction measures in [F3] give $\int d^4x\,d^4\theta\,U=\int d^4y\,d^2\theta\,\mathscr P_{\bar\theta}U$: the nilpotent $x$-to-$y$ substitution changes the spacetime integrand only by finitely many total derivatives, removed by [A3], and the two ordered barred derivatives extract its top barred coefficient. In these coordinates $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}$, so the projector is $\bar D_{\dot2}\bar D_{\dot1}$ and has positive supercovariant derivative degree one. No textbook $-\bar D^2/4$ measure factor is assumed: its relation to ordered coefficient extraction depends on the normalization of contracted spinor measures. For the chiral even variation $\delta X$, the barred derivatives annihilate $\delta X$, hence $\mathscr P_{\bar\theta}(X^\dagger\delta X)=(\mathscr P_{\bar\theta}X^\dagger)\delta X$. The D-term variation is therefore $\int d^2\theta\,\delta X\mathscr P_{\bar\theta}X^\dagger$. Direct differentiation of $W_+$ adds $\int d^2\theta\,\delta X(MX+J(\Phi))$. Thus the chiral Euler equation in this ordered-measure convention is $\mathscr P_{\bar\theta}X^\dagger+MX+J(\Phi)=0$. By [A2] only its degree-zero projection is used.

By definition, each $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$ has positive derivative degree $1/2$, so $\Pi_0(\mathscr P_{\bar\theta}X^\dagger)=0$. Applying $\Pi_0$ to the equation in step 1.1 gives $MX+J(\Phi)=0$. Because $M>0$, this scalar linear equation has the unique solution $X_*=-J(\Phi)/M$.

Substitute $X_*$ into the displayed high-energy superpotential. The quadratic and linear heavy terms become $\tfrac12M(J^2/M^2)-J^2/M=-J^2/(2M)$, so $W_+(\Phi,X_*)=W_L(\Phi)-J(\Phi)^2/(2M)$. This is the derivative-free tree-level F-term coefficient map stated in the conclusion.

The interpretation of the finite operator quotient as an on-shell amplitude basis inherits full AC through [A1], but the representative formula in step 3.1 is choice-free. By [F4], it supplies only the holomorphic coefficient component of a finite threshold map; it does not establish the selected amplitude equality, the low-energy matching of D-term or derivative coefficients, or any estimate for discarded orders.

derivations.claim: In the threshold theorem set $W_L(\Phi)=y\Phi^3/6$ and $J(\Phi)=g\Phi^2/2$. Then $J^2/(2M)=g^2\Phi^4/(8M)$, which gives the displayed $W_-(\Phi)$.

Since $\mathcal X=\theta^1\theta^2F_{\mathcal X}$, the coefficient of $\theta^1\theta^2$ in $\mathcal X\Phi^3$ is $F_{\mathcal X}\phi^3$: [F3] gives the lowest component $\phi$ of $\Phi$, while every positive-$\theta$ component of $\Phi^3$ multiplies a repeated odd generator and vanishes. The ordered Berezin integral in [F4] therefore gives $\int d^2\theta\,\Delta W=\kappa F_{\mathcal X}\phi^3/(6\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}})$.

With $[\phi]=1$, $[F_{\mathcal X}]=2$, and $[\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}]=1$, the coefficient $A_{\mathrm{soft}}=\kappa F_{\mathcal X}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ has dimension one and the scalar cubic term has dimension four. For $F_{\mathcal X}\ne0$, the left derivative gives $Q_1(\theta^1\theta^2F_{\mathcal X})=\theta^2F_{\mathcal X}\ne0$, so fixing this background breaks rigid supersymmetry. The Ward-identity hypothesis of [F5] then fails, and that theorem supplies no protection claim for the fixed soft coefficient. Full AC is inherited only for the selected operator-equivalence interpretation [A1]; no choice is used in this component calculation. No estimate of the soft coefficient's size follows from its dimension.
